newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SPOT RESIDS STEADY AGAIN DESPITE WEAKER CRUDE.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SPOT RESIDS STEADY AGAIN DESPITE WEAKER CRUDE.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly held steady again Thursday in thin trade, with firmer gas prices and forecasts this week for warmer East Coast weather supporting the complex despite weaker crude.

"We're poised to move up with gas firm, but there's still not a lot of heat and almost no demand," said one cash trader, noting surging East Coast city gate gas prices this week gave resid a significant competitive edge.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices again were stable to higher, with one percent gaining more than a quarter to about the $16 a barrel level, while three percent was unchanged in the low-$15s, traders said.
In New York Harbor, 0.3 percent high pour seemed well supported in the low-$18s after a 70,000-barrel deal late Wednesday at $18.25 (8/25 delivery), but not everyone agreed.

"There's some pricing going on for contract deliveries to a New York utility this month, so high pour has been up, but there's still not a lot of load," said one utility source, referring to reports of an 850,000 barrel August HP buy program for one New York utility.
NYH physical one percent held at about $16, with September one percent paper also talked little changed at $16.20-50.
High sulphurs in New York edged up slightly, with 2.2 percent now pegged on either side of $15.00, traders said.

New York city gate gas prices jumped about a dime Thursday to the low-$2.60s/mmBtu, or $16.57 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was up a similar amount to the high-$2.40s/mmBtu, or about $15.62 a barrel.
